statusText: CME equity futures are halted for fifteen of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk, now framed by fresh regional security alerts and an index rebalance that takes effect at Monday's open.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. headline: US embassies across ten Middle East states issued security alerts after the Riyadh and Yanbu attacks, while the confirmed Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance more than doubles SpaceX's weight to 2.82% effective at Monday's open - two new variables landing into a venue that stays shut until 22:00Z
body:
Fifteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final nine contain the 22:00Z restart, the hour after it and the Asian session that follows. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The session was rotational rather than uniform - the Nasdaq added 0.7% while the Dow closed 95 points lower and the S&P 500 rose 0.2% - on a quarterly triple-witching expiry. Latest-session internals corroborate that split: four of the eight Nasdaq megacaps closed higher and four lower, with a mean change near +0.24%, while semiconductors led and software lagged. That divided internal picture is why no structural Tail amplifier is carried into this window.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and restrictive. The FOMC moved the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. Against that, VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44 inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range, so the options market ended the week without stress pricing. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, though WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because the East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike.

Two items are new to this run relative to the preceding assessment, and they pull in opposite directions. The first is an escalation of official concern: US embassies in ten Middle East countries - Bahrain, Israel, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE - issued security alerts this morning urging heightened vigilance and warning of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruption. Those alerts follow Saturday's two claimed Houthi operations, one against sensitive sites in Riyadh and one against Aramco facilities at Yanbu, where the East-West pipeline terminates. The verified record on outcome has not changed: the coalition says the ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed, the attempts against Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were thwarted, Saudi authorities report no casualties or damage, and the fuel-depot fire near King Khalid International Airport was extinguished, although FlightRadar24 recorded a maximum disruption reading at that airport. Separately, the UN has documented 110 civilian casualties across 31 incidents since the August escalation. The alerts therefore widen the distribution of outcomes without yet establishing a loss of export capacity, and the offsetting supply evidence still stands: US Central Command reported Hormuz oil and LNG throughput over the past fortnight at a six-month high, with more than one billion barrels moved out of the Gulf in roughly two months.

The second new item is index-specific rather than geopolitical. The Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance is confirmed and takes effect at Monday's open, lifting SpaceX from a weight of about 1.28% to 2.82% after its free float was recalculated; the final figure was struck on Friday's close, which helps explain the heavy and uneven expiry tape. More than 200 products tracking the benchmark, with over $800bn in assets including the $482bn Invesco QQQ Trust, must adjust. This is a concentrated passive-flow variable for the Monday cash session rather than a path variable for the hours published here, and it is treated as a known checkpoint rather than a Tail amplifier - mechanical rebalancing turnover is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures.

A weekend that is escalatory and de-escalatory at once remains the classic setup for two-way price discovery at the reopen rather than a persistent one-way path, and under the risk definition used here conflicting evidence lifts Stress ahead of Tail. Stress is published at 30, two points above the previous run, because the regional alert perimeter widened to ten countries while the damage assessment stayed nil and Gulf throughput kept improving. Current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5: no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Confidence is published at 74, one point lower, reflecting that the geopolitical picture became less resolved than the previous assessment judged and that the shared context feed's futures and calendar sections were unavailable this run, against a full set of re-verified primary price, rate and energy marks.

No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. One scheduled Asian variable has already resolved: China held the one-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and the five-year at 3.50% for a sixteenth consecutive month this morning, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey, which removes a potential surprise from the Tokyo hours. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday. The first Monday catalyst, the Goolsbee remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, reaching a window high of 18 at the restart before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first fifteen slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 in the final two slots. Stress opened at 21, held that plateau through the Saturday morning, drifted through 22, 23 and 24 across the afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 shortly after midnight, eased to 25 and then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation headlines landed, settling at 28 in the closing hour. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 79, decayed to a 72 trough at 21:00Z as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Fifteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final nine contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours after it. Cash closed Friday and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for two hours, steps to 6 from 09:00Z, 7 from 11:00Z, 8 at 13:00Z, 9 from 14:00Z, 10 at 16:00Z and then one point per hour to 15 at 21:00Z, reaches the window high of 18 across the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour and then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 and 10 across the Asian session. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced escalation of intent and supply repair at the same time; it returns to normal for the final four hours on the base case that repricing has cleared. The Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective at Monday's open sits just beyond the window and is carried as a checkpoint, not an amplifier.
